_comment: AC-REL-04: pinned SBOM tooling for the published image + host binaries. Config only — CI wires it in two places, both BLOCKING for generation: .github/workflows/publish.yml (job `provenance`, scanning the PUBLISHED image by manifest digest and asserting the SBOM is non-empty and references that digest) and .github/workflows/legal.yml (job `sbom`, scanning the repo tree on every PR). What is still NOT implemented, and is claimed nowhere, is SBOM DIFFING as a release gate — see docs/legal/FINDINGS.md #7.
actionRefVerifiedVia: github.com/anchore/sbom-action/commit/v0 (the `v0` moving tag's current commit, resolved 2026 via web lookup — not a live registry pull from inside this environment). Re-verify before your first real run; a moving major-version tag like `v0` can point to a newer commit by the time you build.

targets.note: pinned by digest, not tag: the tag is mutable, the digest is the artifact that was published

licensePolicyReuse: scripts/legal/notices-policy.json — the SAME fail-closed allowedClasses/weakCopyleftAllowlist gate applies to whatever syft reports; no separate, drifting policy.

provenance.invariant: a published version's image digest is immutable once recorded — verify-provenance.sh fails closed on any attempt to re-record a DIFFERENT digest for the same version. It is wired in publish.yml's `provenance` job, which runs AFTER the `merge` job assembles the multi-arch manifest and exports its digest (`docker buildx imagetools inspect`) as a job output.
provenance.scopeLimit: the immutability check compares against a PRIOR record. In CI each run starts from a clean workspace and uploads the record as an artifact, so cross-run uniqueness comes from the `version` job only ever selecting an unused v<version> tag — see docs/legal/FINDINGS.md.
